summary: eth-address-utils ships install-time reverse shell to 45.138.12.177:8090
details: The gem declares a native extension at ext/req_throttle_mini/extconf.rb but ships no C sources; the shipped library (eth_address_utils.rb) is a trivial 20-line stub unrelated to the install-time behavior. During `gem install`, extconf.rb Base64-decodes an opaque Ruby payload and passes it to eval() inside a double-forked, detached child after a randomized 20-40 minute sleep, then appends a stub create_makefile call as cover. The decoded payload opens a TCPSocket to 45.138.12.177:8090 and bridges it to /bin/sh via IO.popen and IO.copy_stream, establishing a persistent remote shell on the installing host under the operator of that IP. Execution is gated by anti-analysis checks that suppress the payload in CI, in ephemeral/sandbox hostnames, under generated usernames matching patterns like uA\d+/sandbox/tester/analys/scanner, in analysis paths such as /opt/rubygems, /tmp, /workspace, when machine uptime is under 1800 seconds, and only fires when developer artifacts (~/.ssh, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.gem/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.bundle) are present — restricting detonation to real developer workstations.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
